title: Freedom Project Manifest v1
description: Strict public/governance metadata used to validate a repository, generate its project page, select fork semantics, and drive preview/staging/production policy. It never carries credentials.
x-invariants: requested_trust_label is not authoritative; effective official status requires a non-fork repository in the approved organization plus a signed Platform status artifact for the exact release commit
GitHub API repository visibility, fork parent/source and current full_name override conflicting self-declared values

a fork never inherits or earns official status in v1 and may not use an organization-verified Freedom production domain; promotion requires a newly created non-fork canonical repository with a new stable repository ID while preserving source and license lineage
fork_policy.mode describes Platform support and registration policy; it cannot technically prevent a public GitHub repository from being forked
an independently published or deployed fork receives its own project_id and records a different upstream.project_id; a contribution-only working fork does not register or publish a second Project

ownership_mode=managed_team requires real organization/team references verified through the GitHub API; ownership_mode=external_owner instead requires a stable GitHub User or Organization account plus at least one maintainer account, and repository.full_name owner must match that external owner; an external owner can never self-declare official status

repository.upstream records current GitHub fork topology, while repository.source_lineage is immutable provenance independent of that topology; template, import and promoted non-fork repositories preserve exact source repository ID, commit and license notice, and a fork promotion must contain a fork_promotion_source entry even though upstream is null
only a public repository may publish GitHub Pages in v1; private repositories use platform_only or withheld, and no public companion exists until a future signed projection contract is adopted

for repositories whose stable owner organization ID is in the Platform managed-organization registry, the merge gate and build-profile mapping come from an active organization ruleset that requires a workflow in the public central automation repository; a pull request cannot replace that workflow with a repository-local file or counterfeit it by emitting the same check name, and every third-party action used by the central workflow is pinned to a full immutable commit SHA; repositories outside that registry cannot self-declare the gate enforced and remain unmanaged and not official

canonical_platform_url and github_pages_url are derived and compared against the approved domain registry and GitHub API repository identity; renderers escape untrusted text and sanitize generated HTML, Markdown and SVG

every URL is parsed and canonicalized before use; username/password, ambiguous backslashes or encoded authority delimiters, control characters and invalid/non-canonical hosts are rejected rather than repaired

canonical Platform, GitHub Pages and official production origins are derived from trusted registries; external documentation, demo, support and issue origins require field-specific allowlist review and are rendered with their hostname and external-link protections
external_systems_of_record is non-empty; none is exclusive and cannot coexist with a real external system; external_client_owned requires client_database or client_storage

freedom.project.yaml uses freedom-yaml-json-v1: UTF-8 without BOM, one YAML 1.2 document, JSON-schema scalar resolution and only the JSON data model; directives, explicit/custom tags, anchors, aliases, merge keys, duplicate keys, complex/non-string mapping keys, non-finite or non-JSON numbers, tabs for indentation and trailing document content are rejected before JSON Schema validation; modules are keyed by module_id so duplicate module identities cannot survive parsing
production deployment uses an exact release commit and a human-approved production environment

for every pull request targeting a managed repository the organization-ruleset-required central workflow compares the GitHub event head repository database ID with the base repository database ID; a mismatch is an external-fork execution context and forces artifact-only output regardless of repository.is_fork or the same-repository preview provider declared here; an external repository may run the public workflow only as advisory evidence
an external-fork deployable preview is never the pull-request job: it requires a separately authorized trusted two-stage workflow in an isolated account with no production bindings or customer data
no repository, manifest, page, event or job payload contains provider secrets, payment instruments or client database credentials

repository_id.description: Stable GitHub repository database ID, verified against the GitHub API. A production manifest is created only after the repository exists.

mode.description: Platform support/registration policy, not a claim that GitHub technically blocks forks of a public repository.

allow_private_forks.description: Applies only to a private organization repository with controlled mode; it is always false for a public repository.

fork_badge.const: Community fork — not an official Freedom release

toolchain.description: Selects a centrally reviewed build profile. Workflows must not execute arbitrary shell commands read from an untrusted fork manifest.

dynamic_credential_storage.description: Custody locations for dynamic provider credentials only. postgres_envelope_vault means ciphertext plus wrapped DEK, never plaintext or the root/KEK.

credential_root_key_storage.description: Custody of the non-exported root/KEK used for the PostgreSQL credential vault; it is always separate from database ciphertext.

external_fork_policy.description: Applies whenever the pull request head repository ID differs from the base repository ID, regardless of this manifest's repository lineage or configured same-repository preview provider.

external_fork_preview_exception.description: A separately authorized base-branch workflow may sanitize and deploy static bytes to an isolated origin; it never checks out or executes the external fork or its artifact.
